title: Pivot Lanes: lightweight staged rollout composer with scenario snapshots
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Design a compact, fast-to-author ‘staged rollout composer’ (Pivot Lanes) that lets engineers and PMs define canary/A-B/gradual traffic ramps using scenario snapshots. The composer prioritizes quick iteration, readable safety controls, and one-click snapshotting so teams can rehearse rollouts and restore prior scenarios.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-create a safe canary from 20+ minutes to under 5 minutes for common use cases.
- Make rollback and snapshot restore discoverable and testable in-console.
- Surface key risk signals inline (error rate, latency drift, cost delta) while editing traffic lanes.
- Provide exportable scenario snapshots used by the runtime to drive canary policies and by playbooks for incident runbooks.

Scope (this ticket):
- Low-fidelity flows -> interactive mid-fi prototype for review with PM/Eng.
- New composer canvas that supports multiple lanes, percentage knobs, scheduled ramps, and snapshot save/restore.
- Inline risk heatmap that maps lane weight + metric delta to a simple warning tier (ok/warn/stop).
- Handoff-ready tokens: component spec, spacing/grid, tokenized color/alerts, and a short interaction spec for QA.

Out of scope (for later cycles):
- Full rollout simulation engine (will be a follow-up ENG ticket).
- Advanced policy editor for programmatic rollouts (handled in Console SDK roadmap).

Acceptance criteria:
- Editor flows: Create a new staged rollout, add up to 4 lanes, set weights, and schedule a ramp.
- Snapshotting: User can save a named snapshot and restore it to the editor.
- Risk heatmap displays a color state when synthetic traffic or past metrics indicate regression risk.
- Prototype tested in user review with at least 3 engineering teams and 2 PMs; feedback captured.
- Design deliverables: Figma interactive prototype, component spec doc, accessibility notes, and a handoff checklist.
design_decisions: Use a horizontal lane canvas (time on X axis) to make schedule ramps scannable and comparable to existing release timelines.
Keep lane controls shallow (weight slider + percent input + traffic tag) to reduce cognitive overhead for routine canaries.
Expose a compact risk heatmap pill instead of full charts in the composer to avoid blocking the authoring flow; detailed metrics will be accessible via a linked modal.
Snapshots are immutable objects with metadata (name, author, timestamp, linked PR) to support reproducible rollouts and audit trails.
tradeoffs: Compact composer reduces visible metric detail — mitigated by 'view metrics' modal that links to console charts.
Snapshot immutability means users must create a new snapshot for small edits — introduced a 'clone-and-edit' affordance to streamline this.
Inline heatmap uses a simple heuristic (weighted metric delta) to give immediate feedback; may produce false positives which we'll tune using telemetry after launch.
acceptance_criteria: User can create + save a staged rollout with at least 2 lanes and a scheduled ramp.
Saved snapshots are listed in a snapshot drawer and can be restored to the composer with a single click.
Risk heatmap updates when toggling lanes or changing weights and shows one of three states (OK / WARN / BLOCK).
Prototype receives 'usable' or better in at least 5/7 usability test tasks across reviewers.
Component spec includes tokens for spacing, color, and micro-interactions and is ready for engineering handoff.
handoff_tasks: Export Figma components into tokens and annotate interaction microcopy.
Create a small acceptance test plan for QA that covers snapshot restore, inline heatmap change, and percentage slider edge cases.
Attach example runtime payload schema for snapshots (link in artifacts list).
Schedule a 60-minute walkthrough with ENG rollout runtime owners and PM to align on snapshot schema and fallback behavior.
comments: 2025-02-18 Ava Chen: Initial concept sketch uploaded. Focused on shortening authoring time and making rollback more discoverable. Attaching early wireframes.
2025-02-21 Marcos Silva: Reviewed wireframes; suggested collapsing advanced scheduling behind an 'advanced' toggle for single-step canaries. Requesting a prototype by 2025-02-28.
2025-02-24 Priya Nanda (PM): Please add a visible cost delta estimate in the lane header — engineering asked for an opt-in toggle for cost calculation to limit backend usage.
2025-02-26 Design critique: UX team preferred horizontal lane canvas but asked to validate accessibility for keyboard-only flows and ensure slider increments are 1%/0.1% for precision.
2025-03-01 Marcos Silva: Mid-fi prototype uploaded to Figma, initial engineering review flagged snapshot schema fields needed by runtime (added to links).
2025-03-02 Samir Patel (Reliability): Heatmap heuristic looks promising; asked for a fail-safe 'block' state tied to absolute error-rate > X and a circuit-breaker toggle in composer.
2025-03-03 Ava Chen: Addressed feedback — added clone-and-edit affordance, cost toggle, and keyboard interactions. Prototype set to 'In Review' and scheduled stakeholder demo 2025-03-05.
